The excerpts show how to set the embedding model globally, but the LLM line is cut off, so I can't confirm the exact `Settings.llm` code from them.

**Embedding model:** Set `Settings.embed_model`. The docs say: "The most common usage for an embedding model will be setting it in the global `Settings` object, and then using it to construct an index and query." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/models/embeddings.md]

The usage example shows:

```python
from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding
from llama_index.core import Settings

# changing the global default
Settings.embed_model = OpenAIEmbedding()
```

This snippet is from "# changing the global default" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/models/embeddings.md]. If you don't set it, LlamaIndex falls back to OpenAI's default, and the docs say "We recommend doing this for new projects" when you choose a current model explicitly [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/models/embeddings.md].

**LLM:** The excerpts don't show the full `Settings.llm` assignment. They do say the `Settings` object is "a simple singleton object that lives throughout your application. Whenever a particular component is not provided, the `Settings` object is used to provide it as a global default." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/supporting_modules/settings.md]. A migration page also mentions an Ollama-based config for non-OpenAI setups, but the code is truncated [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/supporting_modules/service_context_migration.md]. Setting `Settings.llm` the same way as `Settings.embed_model` is the likely pattern, but check the full Settings documentation to confirm the exact code.
